title: 🏔️💨⚡DERIVATIVE of ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE w.r.t. HEIGHT 🏔️💨⚡
description:
Calculus in the real world! In this 60-second tutorial, we interpret the physical meaning of a derivative at a point, looking at a function f(h) that models atmospheric pressure P (in torr) based on your height h (in kilometers).

The Core Concepts:

The Problem Context: We are given a calculated derivative value of f'(2) = -80.4.

Geometric Interpretation: At a physical height of h = 2 kilometers above sea level, the slope of the tangent line to the pressure curve is exactly -80.4.

Physical Interpretation: More importantly, when you are exactly 2 kilometers high, the instantaneous rate of change of atmospheric pressure with respect to height is -80.4 torr/km.

Breaking Down the Units: The negative sign means pressure is dropping as you go higher. Specifically, at that exact split second of climbing past 2 km, the air pressure is dropping at a rate of 80.4 torr for every 1 kilometer of altitude gained.

Understanding how to attach physical units and interpretations to a derivative value is a heavily tested conceptual milestone in AP Calculus, college calculus, and physics courses.

description:

title: QR Factorization Explained with Example | QR Decomposition | Linear Algebra
description:
In this video, you'll learn how QR factorization (QR decomposition) works and how to find the QR decomposition of a matrix step-by-step. We begin by defining the matrices Q and R, reviewing the properties of orthonormal vectors and orthogonal matrices, and discussing the connection between QR factorization and the Gram-Schmidt process. We then work through a complete example, constructing the matrix Q and computing R=Q^TA to obtain the factorization A=QR.

QR factorization is an important technique in linear algebra with applications in solving linear systems, least squares problems, eigenvalue computations, and numerical methods.

📚 Free Guided Notes:
https://www.understandthemath.com/linear-algebra

🎥 Topics Covered:
• What is QR factorization (QR decomposition)?
• The factorization A=QR
• Orthonormal vectors and orthogonal matrices
• Properties of matrix Q
• Upper triangular matrix R
• Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization
• How to compute R=Q^TA
• Complete QR factorization example
• Applications of QR decomposition

This lesson is ideal for students taking Linear Algebra, Applied Mathematics, Engineering Mathematics, Numerical Linear Algebra, and related mathematics courses.

title: Linear Algebra for Machine Learning: Gaussian Elimination & Matrix Operations
description:
In this second lecture of our Linear Algebra for AI series, we dive deep into the Matrix Picture! 🚀

If you've ever struggled to visualize equations in high dimensions or wondered why a neural network throws a "singular matrix" error, this video is for you. We cover the shift from the Row and Column pictures to full Gaussian Elimination (Gauss-Jordan), explaining how algorithms solve $Ax = b$ at scale. You'll learn about pivots, temporary vs. permanent failures, elimination matrices (E matrices), permutation matrices, and the fundamental laws of matrix algebra.

What you will learn:

00:00 - Introduction & Recap of Row vs Column Pictures
00:34 - The Matrix Picture & Gauss-Jordan Elimination Overview
02:49 - Representing Linear Equations as Ax = B
04:40 - Gaussian Elimination Step-by-Step Example
08:30 - What is an Augmented Matrix?
10:24 - Changing Pivots & Diagonal Elements
13:59 - Back Propagation (Back Substitution) Explained
17:35 - Good vs Bad Equations (Parallel Planes & Vectors)
21:14 - Temporary vs Permanent Failures (Zero Pivots)
23:20 - Mathematical Representation of Elimination
26:37 - Elimination Matrices (E Matrices)
35:00 - Naming Elimination Matrices (E21, E32)
38:40 - Permutation Matrices (Row Swaps)
40:29 - Laws of Matrix Algebra (Commutative & Associative Properties)
44:37 - Identifying if a Matrix has an Inverse
47:09 - Finding the Inverse Matrix using an Augmented Identity Matrix [A | I]
51:10 - The Gauss-Jordan Method to Find Inverses
54:02 - Mathematical Representation of Gauss-Jordan Inverse (E * A = I)

description:

Get the textbook for this course! https://amzn.to/45KYgmA
Business Inquiries: wrathofmathlessons@gmail.com 

We introduce the cofactor expansion definition of the determinant of a square matrix of any size, also called the Laplace Expansion. This recursive definition involves two new terms: minors and cofactors. The minor, Mij, of the entry aij is the determinant of the submatrix remaining when the ith row and jth column are deleted. Then, the cofactor of the entry aij is (-1)^(i+j)*Mij. We'll do an example of finding all cofactors of a 2x2 matrix and using the cofactor expansion to find the determinant of the 2x2 matrix, then we will use the cofactor expansion to find the determinant of a 3x3 matrix along a row and then along a column. #linearalgebra

title: How do rockets move in empty space? 🚀 #learnphysics #science #phys101 #physics #space
description:
Out in deep space there's no air, no ground, nothing to push against. So how does a rocket move at all? The answer is Newton's Third Law. The rocket hurls gas backward, violently, out of its engine — and the gas hurls the rocket forward, with exactly equal force. It doesn't push against the air or the ground. It pushes against its own expelled fuel.

That's the entire secret of spaceflight. Every push is a two-way interaction, so throwing mass one way drives you the other. Without the Third Law, we would never have left the Earth.

Full lesson: Newton's Laws — Physics from Scratch | PHYS 101 Lecture 4

title: Why Are Living Organisms Classified? 🦠 | Biology Basics #neet #nta #biology #winnerspad #neetexam
description:
Have you ever wondered how scientists keep track of the millions of plants, animals, and microbes on Earth? 🌍

In this video, we dive into the basics of Biological Classification. Because every organism differs in size, shape, color, and habitat, studying each one individually is impossible. That’s where taxonomy comes in!

We’ll explain:
🔬 How identification and nomenclature work
🦁 Why organisms are grouped into specific taxons
🌿 How classification reveals the evolutionary relationships between species

Make sure to like, share, and subscribe for more biology breakdowns and study concepts! 📚✨

1. Why are living organisms classified?

A large variety of plants, animals, and microbes are found on earth. All these living organisms differ in size, shape, colour, habitat, and many other characteristics. As there are millions of living organisms on earth, studying each of them is impossible. Therefore, scientists have devised mechanisms to classify all living organisms. These methods of classification are based on rules and principles that allow identification, nomenclature, and finally classification of an organism.
For example, based on certain principles, once an organism is identified as an insect, it will be given a scientific name and then grouped with other similar organisms. Thus, various groups or taxon include organisms based on their similarity and differences. Therefore, the biological classification helps in revealing the relationship between various organisms. It also helps in making study of organisms easy and organized.

title: Mean by Direct Method in Grouped Data | Direct Method Explained Fast #Statistics #Maths #Shorts
description:
Mean by Direct Method made simple! 7 easy steps! Learn how to calculate the mean of grouped data using class marks, frequencies, and the Direct Method formula. Perfect for grouped data and frequency tables
Subscribe to Math Simplified by HM for daily math lessons! : https://www.youtube.com/@MathsimplifiedbyHM

Welcome back to Math Simplified by HM! In today's statistics masterclass, we are tackling one of the most important, must-know concepts for Class 10 math exams: calculating the Mean for grouped data using the Direct Method. If you have ever felt overwhelmed by large numbers or complex frequency tables, this step-by-step mathematical guide is designed to make the entire process simple, clear, and perfectly organized.
We break down the Direct Method into 7 highly manageable steps. It all begins with Step 1: The Blueprint. To accurately find the mean, you need to prepare exactly four columns. In Step 2, you populate the first column with your given Classes (the data intervals). Step 3 is absolutely crucial—calculating the Class Mark ($x_i$). This represents the exact middle of each class interval and is found using the formula: $(\text{Lower Limit} + \text{Upper Limit}) / 2$.
Moving forward, Step 4 involves carefully writing your given Frequencies ($f_i$) into the third column. In Step 5, we do the heavy lifting by multiplying the Class Mark by the Frequency to calculate the Product ($x_i \cdot f_i$) for the fourth column. Step 6, known as The Gathering, requires you to sum up the totals at the bottom of your table. You will need $N$, which is the total sum of frequencies ($\Sigma f_i$), and the total sum of your products ($\Sigma x_i f_i$).
Finally, in Step 7, we bring everything together to reach our final conclusion. We plug our carefully gathered totals into the standard Direct Method Formula: $\text{Mean } \overline{X} = \frac{\Sigma x_i f_i}{N}$. As you work through these statistics problems, remember our closing tip: Don't fear the big numbers; step by step, multiply your hard work ($f_i$) with your talent ($x_i$) to get extraordinary results! Grab your notebook and let's master statistics together.

title: Measures of Central Tendency | Mean, Median & Mode Explained #Statistics #Maths #Class10
description:
Master Central Tendency with the Big Three: Mean, Median, and Mode! 📊 Learn how to find the center of any data set. 
Subscribe for more math lessons: https://www.youtube.com/@MathsimplifiedbyHM

Welcome back to Math Simplified by HM! Today, we’re diving into the essentials of Central Tendency. When dealing with large sets of data, you'll often find that numbers tend to cluster around a central value. This phenomenon is known as the measure of central tendency.
In this video, we cover the three most powerful tools for finding this central value: the Mean, the Median, and the Mode—often referred to as 'The Big Three'.
First, we tackle the Mean. This is simply the arithmetic average of all the observations in your data set. The formula is straightforward: Mean = (Sum of all observations) / (Total number of observations).
Next is the Median, which is the exact middle number of your data set. But remember the golden rule: you must first arrange your scores in ascending order! We'll show you how to find the median whether you have an odd or even number of observations. For an odd number 'n', the median is the (n+1)/2 th term. For an even number, there are two middle numbers, so we find their average.
Finally, we explore the Mode. This is the most popular score in the room—the number that appears most frequently in your data. It's that simple!
Understanding these three measures is crucial for making sense of any ungrouped data. Watch the full video to master these concepts step-by-step. Remember, whether finding the mean, median, or mode, every data set tells a story. Make sure your daily studies are always trending upward!

description:
Most traders look at reports and statistics.

I do too.

The reports showed a losing trade, but they did not explain why it happened.

When I reviewed the note, I noticed I had taken a momentum setup at 3:30 AM.

The setup itself was valid.

The timing was not.

A good setup in the wrong environment can still be a bad trade.

Since then, time of day has become part of my checklist before every entry.

Sometimes the answer is not hidden in the statistics.

In this YouTube Shorts video, we explain what Pandas is and why it is one of the most important Python libraries for anyone working with data.
Pandas is widely used for data analysis and data manipulation. It allows you to work with data in a table-like format, similar to Excel, but with the power and flexibility of Python. With Pandas, you can read CSV and Excel files, clean messy datasets, filter rows, select columns, remove missing values, calculate averages, sort information, and analyze large amounts of data quickly.
The main data structure in Pandas is called a DataFrame. A DataFrame contains rows and columns, making it easy to organize and understand data. Whether you are working with student marks, sales reports, customer records, financial data, or employee details, Pandas can help you process and analyze the information efficiently.
Pandas is commonly used by data analysts, data scientists, machine learning engineers, Python developers, and business analysts. It saves time, reduces manual work, and helps convert raw data into meaningful insights using just a few lines of Python code.

title: Model Evaluation Metrics Explained - Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC & R²
description:
A machine learning model can be "99% accurate" and still be completely useless. This video explains exactly why — and hands you the full toolkit of evaluation metrics, built from first principles.

Accuracy, precision, recall, the F1 score, ROC and AUC, MAE, RMSE and R² — every metric you have heard of is really just a statistic that summarises your model's error distribution. We start from the confusion matrix, run one spam-filter example end to end, expose the accuracy paradox on imbalanced data, work through the precision–recall trade-off and the geometry of ROC curves, then move to regression error and what R² actually measures.

It ends with a simple four-question framework for choosing the right metric for your problem — because the wrong metric can hide a broken model behind an impressive score, and the right one tells you the truth before it ships.

Built for GATE, IIT-JAM, ISI / CMI aspirants and curious learners. No hand-waving — one careful step at a time, on a whiteboard.

title: How to make a DIY USB Light using Arduino Uno R4
description:
Learn how to make a simple DIY USB light using the new Arduino Uno R4 Minima! This easy Arduino beginner tutorial walks you through the exact setup and C++ code needed to turn your development board into a functional, constant-on USB desk lamp with zero complex wiring.

If you are looking for the absolute easiest Arduino project to test your breadboard, your LED polarity, or your digital output pins, this 1-minute electronics guide is perfect for you. No shifting delays, no complex math loops—just pure power to Pin 9!

Code used in this video is 

const int ledPin = 9;
void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);
}
void loop() {}


🔌 WIRING LAYOUT & CONNECTION GUIDE
To get your DIY USB Light glowing safely, follow this quick pin-by-pin layout. Because you aren't using a motor or any heavy components, you can plug this circuit safely and directly into your Arduino R4.

Digital Pin 9 connects to the Anode (Long Leg) of the LED

Cathode (Short Leg) of the LED connects to one side of the 220-ohm Resistor

GND Pin connects to the Other side of the 220-ohm Resistor

🛠️ Step-by-Step Assembly
The LED Position: Place your LED into the center grid of your breadboard. Note which row holds the longer leg (Anode / +) and which row holds the shorter leg (Cathode / -).

The Signal Wire: Run a jumper wire from Digital Pin 9 on your Arduino directly into the row containing the longer leg of the LED.

The Current Limiter: Plug one leg of your 220-ohm resistor into the row containing the shorter leg of the LED.

The Ground Return: Plug the remaining leg of the resistor into a different row, and run a jumper wire from that row straight back to any pin labeled GND on your Arduino.

🛠️ MATERIALS USED:
Arduino Uno R4 Minima
5mm LED (Frosted/Diffused)
220-ohm Resistor
Jumper Wires
Switch

title: Ever wondered how billions of transistors inside a chip work together perfectly?
description:
Just imagine a classroom where students enter randomly and teachers start at different times total chaos.
That’s exactly what happens in digital circuits without a clock signal.

In VLSI, the clock acts like a master coordinator ⏱️
It synchronizes every operation by deciding:

✔️ When circuits should start
✔️ When data should move
✔️ When operations should stop

Without proper timing, even the smartest processor can fail.

description:
Every computer, smartphone, and AI system runs on one tiny invention: the transistor.

But how can a microscopic piece of silicon control the entire digital world?

In this engineering deep dive, we explore how transistors actually work — from semiconductor physics and PN junctions to modern MOSFET architecture used inside CPUs and GPUs. You’ll see how a simple electronic switch became the foundation of modern computing.

Today, modern processors contain tens of billions of transistors operating at nanometer scale — powering everything from smartphones to artificial intelligence.

If you want to understand how computers really work, this is where the story begins.

title: Laplace Transforms in Circuits
description:
Capacitors and inductors produce differential equations in the time domain.
Capacitor: i = C dv/dt. Inductor: v = L di/dt.
Combine them in a circuit and you get a system of differential equations. Painful to solve by hand.
The Laplace transform converts the time domain to the s domain.
Differentiation becomes multiplication by s. Integration becomes division by s.
Differential equations become algebra. Solve normally.
Then inverse Laplace back to the time domain to get your answer.
In the s domain, capacitor impedance is 1/sC, inductor is sL, resistor stays R.
Every circuit analysis technique still works - voltage divider, KVL, KCL - just in the s domain.

🚀 100% मुफ़्त – ArcadeDB Fundamentals सीखें और निःशुल्क सर्टिफिकेशन प्राप्त करें!

इस शुरुआती (Beginner-Friendly) और संपूर्ण कोर्स के माध्यम से ArcadeDB Fundamentals सीखें और जानें कि एक उच्च-प्रदर्शन (High-Performance) मल्टी-मॉडल डेटाबेस का उपयोग करके शक्तिशाली एप्लिकेशन कैसे बनाए जाते हैं। चाहे आप डेवलपर हों, छात्र, डेटा इंजीनियर या डेटाबेस के शौकीन, यह कोर्स आपको ArcadeDB को शुरुआत से समझने में मदद करेगा।

## 📌 ArcadeDB क्या है?

ArcadeDB एक ओपन-सोर्स मल्टी-मॉडल डेटाबेस मैनेजमेंट सिस्टम है, जो Graph, Document, Key-Value और Vector जैसे विभिन्न डेटा मॉडल को एक ही डेटाबेस इंजन में सपोर्ट करता है। इसे उच्च प्रदर्शन, स्केलेबिलिटी और लचीलापन (Flexibility) को ध्यान में रखकर बनाया गया है, ताकि डेवलपर्स बिना अलग-अलग डेटाबेस इस्तेमाल किए विभिन्न प्रकार के डेटा को आसानी से प्रबंधित कर सकें।

## 📌 मल्टी-मॉडल डेटाबेस क्या होता है?

मल्टी-मॉडल डेटाबेस वह डेटाबेस होता है जो एक ही प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पर कई प्रकार के डेटा मॉडल को सपोर्ट करता है। अलग-अलग Graph, Document या Key-Value डेटाबेस इस्तेमाल करने के बजाय, आप एक ही डेटाबेस में इन सभी प्रकार के डेटा को मैनेज कर सकते हैं, जिससे एप्लिकेशन डेवलपमेंट अधिक सरल और प्रभावी बन जाता है।

## 💼 ArcadeDB के उपयोग (Use Cases)

🔹 नॉलेज ग्राफ़ और आपस में जुड़े डेटा (Connected Data)
🔹 सोशल नेटवर्किंग एप्लिकेशन
🔹 रिकमेंडेशन इंजन (Recommendation Systems)
🔹 फ्रॉड डिटेक्शन सिस्टम
🔹 पहचान और एक्सेस प्रबंधन (Identity & Access Management)
🔹 सप्लाई चेन और लॉजिस्टिक्स ट्रैकिंग
🔹 नेटवर्क और इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर मैनेजमेंट
🔹 AI और सेमांटिक डेटा एप्लिकेशन
🔹 कंटेंट मैनेजमेंट सिस्टम (CMS)
🔹 कस्टमर रिलेशनशिप मैनेजमेंट (CRM)
🔹 मास्टर डेटा मैनेजमेंट
🔹 रियल-टाइम एनालिटिक्स और बिजनेस इंटेलिजेंस

## 👨‍💻 यह कोर्स किन लोगों के लिए है?

* सॉफ़्टवेयर डेवलपर्स
* डेटाबेस एडमिनिस्ट्रेटर्स (DBAs)
* डेटा इंजीनियर्स
* फुल स्टैक डेवलपर्स
* बैकएंड इंजीनियर्स
* छात्र और शुरुआती शिक्षार्थी
* AI एवं मशीन लर्निंग के उत्साही
* Graph और Multi-Model डेटाबेस में रुचि रखने वाला कोई भी व्यक्ति

## 🔥 ArcadeDB क्यों सीखें?

✅ ओपन-सोर्स और डेवलपर-फ्रेंडली
✅ एक ही इंजन में कई डेटा मॉडल का समर्थन

What is Sqlconf.dll and why these errors keep happening? Technically speaking, Sqlconf.dll is a system-level library used by SQL Server Configuration API to share logic across supported processes. Errors can occur when a setup process doesn’t finish correctly or required files aren’t present.

What is Sqlconf.dll? The SQL Configuration library. It manages unmanaged localized routines for reading and writing SQL Server instance configuration manifests. Essential for localized database service initialization and tuning.

title: How To Enable Auto Delete Old Worktrees In Git Codex Workspace 2026: Complete Step By Step Guide
description: Welcome back to ProgrammingKnowledge2! In today’s highly requested, full-length software engineering tutorial, we are tackling a major storage management and version control configuration: how to enable the Auto Delete Old Worktrees setting for Git inside your ChatGPT Codex Workspace.In 2026, utilizing parallel AI agents is the standard for modern development. When you ask Codex to run a background task, it automatically generates a temporary Git worktree under the hood. This ensures that the AI can compile code on a separate branch without interfering with your main checkout. However, there is a massive hidden downside. Every single one of those temporary worktrees duplicates your repository files, dependencies, and build caches. If you are a final-year B.Tech CSE student running dozens of isolated Kali Linux cybersecurity scripts, or a Product Analyst executing heavy repository updates during a fast-paced product sprint at Dhwani Rural Information Systems right here in Gurugram, these background folders will quietly eat up hundreds of gigabytes of your hard drive space.  To prevent your local disk from maxing out, you must configure Codex to clean up after itself. Let us walk through the exact step-by-step process to automate your worktree deletion and optimize your workspace storage!Step 1: Open the Codex Workspace Configuration MenuTo get started, launch your standalone ChatGPT Codex desktop application. Once your main integrated development environment loads, look toward the top right navigation header and click on the Gear icon. You can also use the standard keyboard shortcut by pressing Command plus comma on macOS or Control plus comma on Windows. This will instantly launch your master Settings dashboard.Step 2: Navigate to the Git and Version Control SettingsInside the master configuration overlay, look at the left-hand menu pane. Scroll past the appearance and agent runtime options until you find the tab specifically labeled Git. Click on this tab. This is your primary command center for configuring how the Codex AI interacts with your local repositories, branch naming rules, and background directory management.Step 3: Locate the Worktree Cleanup ConfigurationScroll down through the Git settings panel until you reach the section titled Worktree Management. By default, Codex leaves all temporary, agent-created worktrees intact on your local drive just in case you want to revisit an old thread later. To change this behavior, look for the toggle switch or checkbox explicitly labeled Auto-Delete Old Worktrees. Click the toggle to activate it.  Step 4: Setting the Retention TimeframeOnce the Auto-Delete toggle is enabled, a secondary dropdown menu will appear asking for your retention policy. You can instruct the Codex engine to prune and delete abandoned worktrees after a specific time limit. For maximum storage efficiency, set this dropdown to 7 Days. This means if an AI thread has been inactive for a week, Codex will automatically run a Git prune command, safely deleting the background worktree folder and freeing up massive amounts of storage space. It is important to note that this only affects Codex-managed background worktrees; any permanent worktrees you manually created from the sidebar will remain completely untouched. title: History Repeats Itself | Dark History Documentary
description:
🔥 HUMAN NATURE REVEALED IN HISTORY! 🔥

In the vast expanse of human history, a peculiar phenomenon has been observed: the repetition of historical events. Ancient Western thinkers like Cicero, Seneca, and Aristotle noted the cyclical nature of civilizations, comparing their rise and fall to the life cycle of a person. This metaphor resurfaced in the 19th-century writings of Herbert Spencer and Émile Durkheim, who also observed the inevitability of historical patterns. Meanwhile, Eastern thought expressed a similar idea through the Mandate of Heaven, which held that unjust rulers would inevitably lose divine support and be overthrown.

The shocking truth is that history does indeed repeat itself, not in exact repetition, but in recognizable cycles and analogies that persist across ages. This phenomenon has been famously asserted by George Santayana, who said that “history repeats itself,” a sentiment echoed in popular aphorisms such as Mark Twain’s observation that “history doesn’t repeat itself, but it does rhyme.” The escalation of historical events, the rise and fall of empires, and the persistence of human nature all point to a deeper truth about the human condition.

The philosophical lesson that can be gleaned from this phenomenon is that human nature remains a constant, despite the changing times and circumstances. The same desires and passions that drove ancient civilizations to greatness and destruction are still present today, shaping the course of human events. This realization should prompt us to reflect on our own place in the grand narrative of history and to consider the wisdom of those who have come before us. As we navigate the complexities of our own time, we would do well to remember that history is not just a series of dusty relics, but a living, breathing guide to the human condition.

title: MARCO POLO's Departure | Mini History Documentary  #history #kublaikhan #marcopolo #historyfacts
description:
Welcome to Mini History. A fresh look on Ancient History's most fascinating tales!

He crossed the known world—and changed how Europe understood it forever.

In 1271 AD, a seventeen-year-old Venetian merchant stepped onto a wooden pier and sailed east—toward deserts that sang, cities larger than any Europe had known, and an empire that ruled half the earth.

This is the true story of Marco Polo.

From the markets of Venice to the court of Kublai Khan, Marco Polo spent 24 years crossing deserts, oceans, and empires—serving the Mongol court, witnessing inventions centuries ahead of Europe, and recording a world that many would refuse to believe existed.

Captured in war and imprisoned, he dictated his memories into a book that would reshape maps, ignite imaginations, and inspire explorers for centuries—including Christopher Columbus.

This episode explores:
 • The Silk Road and the Mongol Empire at its height
 • Cities of unimaginable scale and wealth
 • Paper money, coal, porcelain, and global trade networks
 • Why Marco Polo was called a liar—and why history proved him right
 • How one traveler stitched East and West together with words

Discovery is not about arriving somewhere new…
It’s about returning changed.

What began as a trade deal turned into one of history’s darkest bargains — a nation flooding another with addiction, all in the name of profit. This is the forgotten story of how ambition disguised itself as progress, and how a simple plant reshaped the fate of two great civilizations.

Yet behind the smoke and the silver, a deeper question lingers — what happens when “civilization” itself becomes the weapon? The answer would come in gunfire, treaties, and a war fought not for freedom, but for the right to sell despair. The story ends where the world’s balance begins to shift… and where mercy becomes the most expensive thing of all.

title: TWO GAS STATION, SAME FUEL BUT PRICE DIFFERENCE WHY?
description:
opportunity cost 
Most people think the cheaper option is always the smarter choice. But what if saving a few dollars on gas actually costs you something more valuable?
This is the idea behind Opportunity Cost — one of the most important concepts in economics. Every decision comes with a hidden cost: the value of the next best alternative you give up.
In this example, two gas stations sell the same fuel at different prices. The cheaper station seems like the obvious choice... until you consider the time, effort, and opportunities you sacrifice to get there.
Economics isn't just about money. It's about choices.

title: A brief introduction to Russian psychology: Georgy Chelpanov
description:
A brief introduction to Russian psychology 
Georgy Chelpanov was the founder of Russian psychology and one of the pioneers of experimental psychology in Russia. This short documentary explores his life, ideas, and legacy.

Georgy Chelpanov (1862–1936) is widely regarded as the father of Russian psychology. As the founder of the first Psychological Institute in Russia and a pioneer of experimental psychology, he played a crucial role in establishing psychology as a scientific discipline.
Yet despite his immense contributions, Chelpanov remains largely unknown outside academic circles. This short film explores the life, work, and legacy of a scholar who helped shape the foundations of modern psychological science in Russia.
Who was Georgy Chelpanov? How did his ideas influence generations of psychologists? And why has his name faded from public memory?
This documentary offers a concise introduction to one of the most important figures in the history of psychology.

title: Being and Logos - Introduction to Middle-Platonism - 4 of X - Antiochus of Ascalon
description:
Welcome to Being & Logos - An Introduction to Middle-Platonism

While Plotinus and his inheritors are often associated with western mysticism and the occult philosophy, the philosophical ferment of the centuries following the Old Academy (post 347 bce) most directly influenced Hermeticism, Gnosticism, Hellenistic Magic and Astrology, Alexandrian Judaism and early Christianity.  This period of philosophy, denoted as “Middle Platonism,” is thus crucially important for the study of the development Western Esotericism and, surprisingly (or not), this period is woefully unappreciated.  This seminar aims to be an introduction to Middle-Platonism (c. 100 bce - c. 200 ce), specifically with an eye toward developments in metaphysics.  Along with deepening our appreciation of the development of western philosophy, my hope is that we come to better appreciate the philosophical dimensions of Hermeticism, Gnosticism, Hellenistic Magic and Astrology, Alexandrian Judaism, early Christianity, Neo-Platonism and Western Esotericism more widely.

Welcome to Being & Logos - An Introduction to Middle-Platonism

title: 1 Intro to NAVIGATIONAL MIND unscripted: KINETICS, KONSTELLATION & KEDOS #hippocampus #philosophy
description:
#navigational #philosophy #mind INTRODUCTION: #KINETICS #KONSTELLATION #KEDOS
Navigational Approach to Mind
https://open.substack.com/pub/communityphilosophy/p/the-navigational-approach-to-mind
As an exploration of the mind through the lens of embodied science, the Navigational Philosophy of Mind presents a novel approach to understanding our consciousness. Unlike traditional computational models, this perspective emphasizes the mind as a navigational system, informed by three interconnected principles: Kinetics, Konstellation, and Kedos.

Three K's: Foundations of Navigational Mind:
Hi, everyone. Welcome to an insightful journey into the 'Three K’s'—Kinetics, Konstellation, and Kedos. These concepts are integral to the navigational approach to embodied science and cognition, a field that redefines how we perceive and study the mind.

Our aim is to move beyond traditional frameworks that have historically focused on binary oppositions—either computational or connectionist models—and towards a more fluid understanding. This introductory discussion provides an overview of these ideas, setting the stage for a more in-depth exploration through a series of videos and writings.

Kinetics: The Movement of Mind

Kinetics, familiar to many as movement, serves as the first cornerstone of our navigational approach. Consider the myriad movements around and within us: the dance of trees in the breeze, the stirrings of life within our own bodies, and the ceaseless dance of molecules and atoms. By framing the mind as a series of movements, we simplify our understanding of a wide variety of life forms. This kinetic perspective helps us transcend binary thinking, offering a unifying theme for the multiplicities of thought and existence.

Konstellation: From Binary to A System of Stars

The second principle, Konstellation, encourages us to shift from binary thinking to a constellation-like view. Rather than focusing on opposites, a Konstellation includes multiple points of view and relational positions. By visualizing our world as a constellation—a network of interrelated parts—each position yields different oppositions and insights. This perspective empowers us to think in dimensions beyond the linear, embracing the complexities of 3D, 4D, or even 5D perspectives in understanding our mind and philosophies.

Kedos: The Primordial Urge 

Finally, we delve into Kedos, or care, representing the physical and emotional pull at the heart of our inquiry into the mind. This complex term embodies concern, love, and the foundational urge that drives our quest for knowledge. In understanding Kedos as the ontological essence of life’s movements, we capture the dynamic tension between need and fulfillment. As a verb, Kedos signifies action—a compelling force of connection and creation within the constellation framework.

Holding Paradox into a New Way of Thinking

The navigational philosophy of mind invites us to move beyond our traditional, often constrictive viewpoints. By emphasizing movement, relational networks, and care, this approach offers a more expansive and inclusive understanding of knowing and being. When we listen to multiple voices within the Konstellation, we gain new perspectives that can lead us to healthier, more supportive ways of living.

As we embark on this journey together, consider the ways these principles might transform your own understanding of mind and meaning. The introductory video series linked below will delve into each of these principles in greater depth: 

1. Kinetics: Exploring the movement as a foundation for understanding the mind.
2. Konstellation: Embracing the multi-dimensional networks of knowledge.
3. Kedos: Examining care as the fundamental urge for understanding.

I invite you to engage with these ideas, share your thoughts, and follow along for more philosophical insights into the way our world navigates consciousness. As we constellate with care and curiosity, we shape new pathways for thought and connection. Let’s explore these together—watch, reflect, and discover. Stay curious, stay connected.

With the implementation of NEP 2020, discussions around teaching quality, student-centred learning, and holistic education are increasing across India. But one silent factor continues to shape classroom outcomes every day: teacher expectations.

title: James Hillman: Is Your Rage Actually Outrage?
description:
Is the rage you are feeling a political instinct, actually?  In this clip by Dr. Brian Lippincott, we see one of his mentors, James Hillman, the founder of archetypal psychology, explore the concept of "outrage." 

He challenges traditional therapy's focus on our sexual or relational instincts while ignoring Aristotle's idea that man is fundamentally a "political animal." 

If we ignore our political instincts and our reactions to the world around us, we risk becoming disordered.  

Dive deeper into the work of James Hillman and analytical psychology in our full-length primer lectures every Tuesday and Thursday!
🔗 @BrianLippincott-phd 

 Hillman argues we have to know when we are furious at the world to be a "full animal being." Do you agree that our political instincts are ignored in modern therapy? Let's discuss below! 👇


Hillman Transcript: "What is this rage I feel over so much that happens? I'm angry, whatever happened to me in the past. But maybe the rage is outrage. Maybe it wants to be out. Maybe it is a political reaction to the world, to what's going on. Aristotle said a very famous sentence: man is by nature a political animal. Now, we look in therapy at a person and say he's a sexual animal or he's a relational animal or whatever, and that work we go at. But do we go at his being a political animal, and that part of his instinctual life is political? And if that instinctual life isn't paid attention to, he can be disordered. You've got to be political to be a full animal being. And to be a full animal being means you have to know when you're afraid of the government or of whatever, and you have to know very well when you are furious."

#JamesHillman #ArchetypalPsychology #DepthPsychology #MentalHealth #Philosophy #Outrage

title: Existential Sex Therapy: Reading Desire as Existential Information
description:
What if low desire isn't a dysfunction — it's a message?
In this excerpt from her 2-hour CE workshop, Existential Sex Therapy: Reading Desire as Existential Information, Genevieve Marcel, PhD, introduces a paradigm shift for clinicians working with women who present with low or absent desire and nothing measurably wrong.
Drawing on existential philosophy and clinical practice, Dr. Marcel reframes desire not as a deficit to be corrected, but as psychological communication — a signal worth listening to rather than a symptom to suppress.
This course explores five existential themes — freedom, isolation, meaning, mortality, and authenticity — as a clinical architecture for understanding what a woman's desire may be trying to say.
🎓 This is a 2-hour CE course available through MSTI.

In the full course, you'll learn how to:

— Distinguish the dysfunction model from an existential, meaning-centered approach

— Identify which existential theme is most active in a client's presentation

— Apply reframing questions directly in session

📚 Dr. Marcel's forthcoming book, Existential Sex Therapy for Women: A Meaning-Centered Approach (Routledge, Taylor & Francis), expands on the clinical framework introduced in this workshop.

Do you feel like you are constantly battling an invisible force keeping you from reaching your financial goals? You are not alone. In this video, I break down why traditional budgeting methods often fail because they ignore the biological reality of how your brain processes money. If you are tired of the cycle of impulse buying, emotional spending, and chronic overspending, this deep dive into behavioral finance is for you.
We will explore the dopamine-driven feedback loops that retailers and tech companies use to exploit your biology. I explain why the "one-click" checkout button and targeted social media ads are engineered to bypass your logic and force you into a state of compulsive consumption. By understanding compensatory spending and identity-based financial decisions, you can finally take back control of your bank account.
This isn't just another lecture on austerity or cutting lattes; it’s a practical, actionable toolkit for building friction, managing your emotional triggers, and realigning your financial habits with your actual values. I am teaching you how to outsmart the algorithms and stop using money as a temporary fix for underlying feelings. Learn to identify your specific spending triggers, implement effective cooling-off periods, and cultivate long-term financial discipline that actually lasts. Stop blaming yourself and start building a system that works for your human brain.

title: Civics-Short: How do Municipal Elections work in South Africa?
description:
In this Civics-Short we explain how elections for municipal councils work. This clip is part of our Civics Academy Election Series which explores different aspects of elections, and why they are a central feature of democracy.

Metropolitan, local and district councils determine municipal policies, budgets and bylaws. They must see to it that services are delivered and public funds are spent wisely.

The Electoral Commission of South Africa organises the elections and ensures that they are free and fair. Voting in municipal elections is allowed only at a voting station in the voting district where you are registered.

There are eight metropolitan municipalities, each divided into wards. Half of the Metro Councillors are ward councillors and the other half are proportional representation or PR councillors. So if you live in a metro, you receive two ballot papers on election day. One to choose your ward councillor and one to choose your preferred political party. If you live outside a metro, you receive three ballot papers on Election Day. One to choose your ward councillor, one to choose your preferred political party for the local council, and one to choose your preferred political party for the district Council.

If your preferred ward candidate did not win, did your vote go to waste? No, because the votes for candidates that belong to a party and who didn't win are used to calculate that party's representation on the council. So even if your preferred ward candidate did not win, your vote helps his or her party to gain PR seats. Councillors are elected for five years.

By voting, you help determine who will lead your municipality.

title: What is democracy?#politics#democracy#government#shortsfeed
description:
what is democracy ? it's meaning in easy language 

Civics with Clarity , 🛑 
 

*MEANING:*  
Democracy means rule by the people.  
Greek words: Demos = People, Kratos = Power.  
One line: Democracy is a government where people choose their leaders and take part in decisions.  
Famous quote: Abraham Lincoln – "Government of the people, by the people, for the people."

*MAIN FEATURES / POINTS OF DEMOCRACY:*  

1. By the People:  
   People elect the government through voting.  
   Example: Elections in India every 5 years.

2. For the People:  
   Government works for welfare of citizens.  
   Example: Free education, health schemes.

3. Of the People:  
   Leaders come from common people, not royal family.  
   Example: Any citizen can become Prime Minister.

4. Universal Adult Franchise:  
   All adults aged 18 years and above can vote.  
   No discrimination of caste, gender, religion, money.

5. Fundamental Rights:  
   People get freedom of speech, religion, equality.  
   Example: You can criticize the government.

6. Rule of Law:  
   Law is equal for everyone.  
   Even President and PM must follow law.

7. Majority Rule with Minority Rights:  
   Decisions by majority, but minority groups are protected.  
   Example: Reservation system in India.

8. Free and Fair Elections:  
   Elections without cheating.  
   Conducted by Election Commission. Example: Use of EVM and VVPAT.

9. Independent Judiciary:  
   Courts are free from government control.  
   Example: Supreme Court can cancel unconstitutional laws.

10. Tolerance and Discussion:  
    Different opinions are allowed.  
    Problems solved by debate in Parliament

*IMPORTANCE OF DEMOCRACY:*  
1. Gives freedom to people.  
2. Protects basic rights.  
3. Government is answerable to people.  
4. Change of power happens peacefully through elections.

title: From Timeline To Threads: How Civics Really Works
description:
A timeline can tell you what happened. It can’t always tell you what it meant, or why the meaning keeps changing.

We’ve spent months building a foundation in civics: the Declaration of Independence and its claims about equality, unalienable rights, and consent; the Constitution and its structure; and the core mechanics of American government like separation of powers, checks and balances, federalism, and the rule of law. We’ve followed those ideas as they collide with reality through Supreme Court cases, political parties, and moments of national crisis from the early republic through the modern presidency. But there’s a problem with treating political history as a straight line: the closer you are to events, the harder it is to separate reaction from impact.

So we’re making a deliberate shift. Instead of racing forward president by president, we’re slowing down and pulling on threads that cut across time, focusing on the people, relationships, and recurring conflicts that reveal how power actually works. Expect episodes that lean into historical drama and civic insight: iconic rivalries like Hamilton vs Burr, the complicated bond between Adams and Jefferson, the politics of image around figures like Jackie Kennedy, and stories that sit outside the spotlight but reshape civic life. We’ll also widen the lens with themes like Juneteenth and gerrymandering through place and geography, while building toward a big question that ties the whole project together: what does the Declaration mean 250 years later?

If you want civic education that helps you make sense of the present, not just memorize the past, come with us into this next phase. Subscribe, share the show with a friend, and leave a review telling us which rivalry or overlooked figure you want us to cover next.

title: How Treaties Work | Simple Civics
description:
A treaty is a written agreement between two or more nations. But who enforces them?
 
There are 195 countries, all playing in the same sandbox that is planet Earth. Each one is a sovereign entity, meaning no higher authority governs them. However, they also need to work together! One of the primary methods of diplomacy used for international agreements comes in the form of treaties. Find out how treaties work, as well as how they are enforced, in this episode of Simple Civics.

title: Grade 9 Civics & Government | Comparative Governments | Democracy, Monarchy & Dictatorship Explained
description:
In this Grade 9 Civics & Government lesson, students explore how different types of governments work around the world. The video introduces comparative government, helping learners understand how political systems organize power, make decisions, and protect citizens’ rights.

We begin by defining government and why societies need it — to create order, provide services, and ensure justice. Then we compare major government types:

Democracy, where people rule through elections and participation

Monarchy, where power is held by a king or queen

Dictatorship, where authority is controlled by one leader or small group

Oligarchy and Theocracy, where religion or elite groups influence rule

Students will explore real-world examples like the United States (democracy), Saudi Arabia (monarchy), and North Korea (dictatorship) to see how power and freedoms differ.

We also discuss how governments handle laws, economic policies, and citizen involvement. Learners discover that while systems vary, all share one purpose — maintaining stability and serving the people.

By the end, students will:
✅ Identify and compare major forms of government
✅ Understand how leadership and power differ globally
✅ Analyze the advantages and challenges of each system
✅ Appreciate the importance of citizen participation

This topic builds global awareness and critical thinking, showing how every nation’s system reflects its history, culture, and values.

title: Pronunciation Practice: The Spanish /b/ Sound
description:
Spanish pronunciation made simple. In this quick lesson, you will learn how to pronounce the Spanish letters b, v, and w. The RAE eliminated any distinction inherited from Latin, so b and v are homophones (with w joining them in specific borrowed words). Specifically, Spanish features the occlusive [b] and the approximant [β], which are allophones of the same /b/ phoneme; they do not change the meaning of a word.

Example sentences (English Translation): 
An old friend of Braulio's is coming on Friday. 
Abelardo travels by boat and takes his bicycle. 
The good neighbor swept the trash off the sidewalk. 
Belén is looking for a cheap scarf.  
Boris sells vegetables on Thursday and Saturday mornings.

title: It's time we go VS It's time we went | Common Spoken English Mistakes | English With Ananya
channelName: Learn English | Let's Talk - Free English Lessons
description:
Do you say "It's time we go" or "It's time we went"? If you're confused about which one is correct, you're not alone! This is one of the most common spoken English mistakes that non-native speakers make. In this comprehensive grammar lesson, we'll reveal the exact rule behind this confusing construction and teach you why native speakers always use one form over the other!

👉All Online English Course Details - 
https://www.letstalk.academy/s/store
OR 
👉Send 'HI' on WhatsApp no - +919324246223

Video Overview:
This detailed English tutorial explores a frequently confused grammatical structure involving the subjunctive mood. You'll learn why "It's time we went" is correct while "It's time we go" is considered incorrect in English. Whether you're a beginner learning basic English grammar or an advanced learner wanting to perfect your spoken English, this video will eliminate all confusion about this common mistake!

Why This Video Matters:
This is one of the most common spoken English mistakes because it seems illogical to English learners. You might think "time is present, so use present tense" (we go), but English grammar works differently! The verb form used after "it's time" actually follows the subjunctive mood rule, which uses the past tense to express something that isn't yet reality. Understanding this rule will significantly improve your spoken English accuracy!

What You'll Learn in This Video:
✓ Complete explanation of "It's time we went" - why this is correct
✓ Why "It's time we go" is incorrect in standard English
✓ Understanding subjunctive mood in English
✓ Why English uses past tense for future/present situations
✓ Similar structures: "It's high time," "It's about time"
✓ Related expressions using subjunctive mood
✓ Real-world examples in natural English conversations
✓ How native speakers use this construction
✓ Common mistakes English learners make
✓ When to use this structure in professional and casual English
✓ Practice examples and correct usage patterns
✓ Why the rule exists in English
✓ Regional variations in British vs American English
✓ Advanced subjunctive mood applications
✓ Similar constructions that follow the same rule

The Complete Rule Explained:
CORRECT FORM: "It's time we went"
Structure: "It's time" + Subject + Past Tense Verb

"It's time we went"
"It's time you left"
"It's time they arrived"
"It's time she finished"
"It's time I started"

Why Past Tense?

English subjunctive mood uses past tense to express something that hasn't happened yet
Even though we're talking about a future or present action, we use past tense
This is called the "subjunctive mood" - a special grammatical mood for unreal situations

title: SAT Math Practice Problem | Solve a Polynomial Equation (Step-by-Step)**
description:
In this SAT Math practice problem, we go step-by-step to solve the 4th-degree polynomial equation: $a^4 - 3a^2 - 4 = 0$. To solve this, you need to understand how to factor polynomials, work with exponents, and find complex roots. By the fundamental theorem of algebra, we know this equation has exactly four solutions. 

Watch as we simplify the problem using a technique called quadratic substitution, temporarily replacing $a^2$ with $x$ to create a simple quadratic trinomial ($x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0$). From there, we use the zero product property to find both our real and imaginary roots ($i$)! 

If you are taking the SAT, you don't want to take a chance on a low score because of weak math skills. So instead of guessing on math questions, learn to answer them confidently! Make sure to check out my full SAT math test prep course for comprehensive, easy-to-follow lessons.

SAT Math prep : Equilateral triangle height problem
description:
SAT Math prep : Equilateral triangle height problem

An equilateral triangle has a height of 77√3. What is the length, in units, of one of this triangle?

A)  154√3
B)  154
C)  77√3
D)  77

Learn how to calculate the equilateral triangle side length when you only know the height. This step-by-step guide makes complex geometry simple.

Finding the side length of an equilateral triangle from its height is a common challenge in geometry coursework. If you are struggling with triangle properties or specific math problems involving roots and trigonometry, this breakdown provides the exact method you need to solve these questions quickly.

We start by visualizing the triangle and splitting it into smaller right-angled triangles to establish the correct relationships. By setting the height to 77√3, we walk through the algebraic steps to isolate the variable and find that the total side length is 154. This approach is perfect for students looking to master triangle height formula applications.

Whether you are preparing for an upcoming exam or just brushing up on your geometry skills, understanding these relationships is essential. Use this logic to solve for any triangle side given a known height, no matter the numbers involved.

title: What exactly is an "interval" in music? 📏🎵
description:
In simple terms, an interval is just the distance between any two notes! Think of it like measuring the gap between two steps on a ladder. 🪜
Here is the simple breakdown:
🔢 The Number: We measure them using numbers (like a 2nd, 3rd, or 5th) just by counting the lines and spaces from the bottom note to the top note.
🎭 The Quality: We also give them a "quality" name (like Major, Minor, or Perfect), which describes exactly how that distance sounds and feels.
🧱 The Building Blocks: Intervals are the absolute foundation of all music! Stacking them creates chords, and playing them in a row creates melodies.

In this episode of Wealth on the Move, host Will Hoffman engages with Cary Siegel, author of 'Why Didn't They Teach Me This in School?' They discuss the critical need for financial literacy in education, the importance of teaching children about money management, and practical strategies for parents to fill the gaps in their own financial knowledge. Cary shares insights from his book, emphasizing the value of getting rich slowly, avoiding the pitfalls of comparison, and the necessity of negotiation in everyday life. The conversation highlights the shift from traditional pensions to personal financial responsibility, urging listeners to take charge of their financial futures. In this conversation, Cary Siegel shares invaluable financial wisdom, emphasizing the importance of budgeting, living below one's means, and making informed financial decisions at various life stages. title: Financial Management Basics
description:
“Financial Management, also known as Corporate Financial Management or Managerial Finance, is the process of planning, raising, investing, and controlling funds in a business. Its main purpose is to ensure that money is available and used efficiently. The major areas of financial management are financing decisions, investment decisions, dividend decisions, and working capital management. The primary objective of financial management is wealth maximization, which means increasing shareholders' wealth over the long term. Other objectives include profit maximization, maintaining liquidity, ensuring adequate funds, optimum utilization of funds, proper capital structure, business growth, and risk management. Financial managers use information prepared under IFRS, IAS, and US GAAP for decision-making.”

The lesson is designed for learners who already have some familiarity with the VBA editor, ranges, and variables, and are ready to practice applying those skills in more dynamic, real-world Excel automation scenarios.

What it is: Excel VBA, or Visual Basic for Applications, is the programming language built into Microsoft Office that allows users to automate actions and processes inside Excel and other Office applications. In Excel, VBA can be used to perform simple tasks like changing cell values, formatting data, sorting information, or creating worksheets, but it becomes especially powerful when those actions are connected together into larger automated workflows. With VBA, users can build tools that save time, reduce repetitive work, generate reports, interact with other Office apps, and complete complex tasks at the click of a button.

You’ll also learn how to change properties, write values into cells, align objects, create numbered lists, and use variables inside loops. The lesson also introduces For Next loops and Do Until loops, showing how they can provide more flexibility when working with counters, repeated actions, exit conditions, and more advanced automation logic.

title: WHY YOUR PHOTOS LOOK FLAT (And How to Fix It!) | Tip 46 of 365 #Tips and #Tricks for #Photographers
description:
🚨 WHY YOUR PHOTOS LOOK FLAT (And How to Fix It!) | Tip 46 of 365 Tips and Tricks for Photographers

Have you ever captured an incredible subject, used the right camera settings, and still ended up with a photo that feels dull and lifeless?

The problem might not be your camera.

It might be your light.

In today’s photography tip, you’ll learn one of the most important photography fundamentals that separates beginner photographers from experienced photographers: understanding the direction of light.

Many photographers focus entirely on their subject and camera settings while completely overlooking where the light is coming from. But light does far more than simply illuminate a scene—it creates depth, texture, shape and dimension.

In this video you’ll discover:

📸 Why front lighting often makes photos look flat
📸 How side lighting adds depth and texture
📸 When to use backlighting for dramatic images
📸 How changing your position can instantly improve your photography
📸 Why lighting direction matters more than many camera settings

Whether you’re shooting portraits, wildlife, landscapes, street photography or everyday subjects, understanding light direction will dramatically improve your images.

The next time your photographs feel boring or lack impact, don’t immediately change your aperture, shutter speed or ISO.

Change your position.

Sometimes moving just a few steps can completely transform your image.

description:

Add your image and remove the background if needed. Select the subject again, this time to create the mask.
Add the second image, hold Alt and click to link it to the previous layer.
Mask it, use the soft brush with low opacity to draw over and reveal some areas that work best.
You can change the blending mode of the layer to see if it gives better result.
Add noise and some textures on top.

Done! Your Double Exposure effect is ready!
